app: 10. Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: DON’T FALL FOR THIS APP! NEED A BUG FIXXXXXX! || I’ve appreciated the Finch app for how it supports mental health, builds daily habits, and encourages self-reflection. It’s gentle, positive, and has genuinely helped me stay grounded. But what happened today left me frustrated, confused, and concerned for other users. This morning, my cousin opened Finch and discovered that her streak had been completely reset—two full weeks of progress gone. She hadn’t backed up her iCloud data in two weeks, so there was no way to recover what she lost. It happened without warning, and without any obvious reason. After seeing what happened to her, I decided to take action. I immediately did an iCloud backup on the same day—today—just in case the same issue happened to me. I thought that by backing everything up right away, I could avoid the same mistake and protect my progress. But later today, when I opened Finch, the exact same thing happened to me: my streak reset, and the app showed I had lost three days of progress. I was shocked and confused—especially since I had just backed up everything that morning. Even though the app eventually corrected itself and restored my streak to the right day, the initial reset was upsetting and left me unsure if I could trust that my data was actually safe. What’s especially frustrating is that this happened despite my efforts to protect myself. I saw what happened to someone else, took the right precautions, and the glitch still hit me. That kind of experience makes users feel powerless. I’m not the only one this has happened to, and I worry it could happen to others who might not even realize it until it’s too late. Finch is a wonderful app with a great mission—but losing streaks and progress, especially when users take steps to avoid it, damages trust. People use Finch to build confidence, stay motivated, and feel supported—not to feel stressed about losing their data through no fault of their own. I hope the developers will investigate these reset issues seriously and provide more reliable data protection—so no one has to lose progress they worked hard for, especially not when they’re doing everything right.

app: 10. Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text: PLEASE READ THIS || I’ve been using the Finch app for a while now, and it’s become a comforting part of my daily routine. I love how it helps track self-care, rewards consistency, and builds positive habits. But today, I watched something happen that left me feeling worried, frustrated, and unsure if I can fully trust the app anymore.  Two of my cousins experienced streak resets in Finch—on the same day. One of them hadn’t backed up her iCloud data in two weeks, and when she opened the app, she lost two full weeks of progress. The app gave no warning. She didn’t do anything wrong. It just reset.  After seeing that happen, my other cousin immediately did an iCloud backup— on the same day, just to protect her progress. But even after taking that step, her Finch app still glitched. It reset her streak by three days, and although the app eventually restored it to the correct day, the fact that it happened at all was stressful and confusing. She had done everything right—and it still didn’t stop the glitch.  Watching both of them go through that, on the same exact day, has honestly made me nervous. I haven’t experienced a reset yet, but now I’m scared that I might. I’ve taken steps like backing up my iCloud, but clearly, even that isn’t a guarantee. Seeing two people close to me lose progress like that—despite their best efforts—makes me feel like this could affect anyone.  Finch is such a positive and supportive app, and that’s what makes this so disappointing. Users build emotional connections with their streaks, their routines, and their personal goals. When progress disappears without warning, it’s more than just a technical problem—it’s demotivating and stressful. And if this keeps happening, it could drive people away from an app that’s meant to help them.  I hope the Finch team is paying attention. These glitches aren't isolated—multiple people have written about the same problem happening, with some losing years worth of finch just gone in a minute. Please look into what’s causing this, and give users more reliable protection. Because losing progress—especially when you're trying to do everything right—is a extremely bad thing of a thing that can happen in a mental health app.

app: 20. Habit — Daily Tracker - Crush your goals like a boss
text: 2021 no longer unlimited habits for free || I have used this app through 2019 and 2020. I built 1 new habit every month in 2019 and continued 8 (out of 12) of them in 2020. To say I love this app is an underestimation.  As of my personal app philosophy, I am perfectly fine with paying a one time purchase and major upgrades. Not a fan of paying for subscription. So I definitely don’t like the idea of paying a subscription to access $ More than 9 habits  $ Backup or data export $ Extended notification (which is THE best functionality of this APP if you ask me)  $ Widget.   But I am paying for it today because I’m paying back for the 2 years I have used it for free.

Really like the app || Update: the recent update seems to have broken the glass-by-glass counter of the water category. Now it checks of the activity when I am trying to tick only one glass. And even if I manually mark this task as incomplete, the app completes it itself. Not sure if this has something to do with the sync with Apple Watch, which has been the only thing that has changed for me. But uninstalling the app from the watch has also not helped. Hopefully this gets corrected soon  -  Review besides the bug below:  The concept of streaks is really solid to form habits. It’s a psychological hack, yes, but something that works for me. Mind you an app is not as powerful as a poster in a room, but its the next best thing.  I have had a few apps which track streaks, and this app, Streaks, definitely has the best design that actually is close to checking out things on a poster. And UI really is important to promote usage and habit building.  The cool things which this app does differently which stood out for me: 1: you can set timers for timed activities like 1 hour study or 15 min meditation. 2. Multiple tasks which form an activity can be broken down. For e.g, drinking 10 glasses of water can be checked off one glass at a time. 3. There’s a tie in to health app so you don’t need to check off workouts and other health things.  Overall happy with this app and see myself using it. I have had a few streaks going the last couple of months, but have not been consistent enough. Hope that will change in the coming months.

Life-changing but with a lot more room for improvement || I started using Streaks as a part of my depression combating plan. I needed an app to remind me of the basics of life such as taking a shower, taking vitamins and meds, housekeeping, tracking weight, working out, sleeping on time, drinking water, brushing teeth, enjoying a cup of coffee, reading a book, writing a journal, ..., etc. It has dramatically changed my life in just a couple of weeks. I don't really care about doing streaks, but I desperately needed reminders and a way to keep track of things.  == What I Like == - Integrates well with iOS, WatchOS, MacOS, Apple Health, Apple Shortcuts, and widgets - You can connect "start actions" to Apple shortcuts, which I absolutely love, since I turn related "Focus" modes on (but I can't turn it off, see below) - It allows you to export your data as CSV - Many options for theming  == Needs Improvement == - The UI/UX is an absolute nightmare. It's not intuitive at all. You find what you're looking for if you're lucky. There are surprising elements, random icons, and random numbers all over the place and you have to press everything randomly like a monkey to discover features. It's like they forced themselves to be in a certain visual language/framework, and they lost all sense of common sense. I had (and sometimes still have) a very hard time understanding why I have different sections, what is the icon on top for, how to reorder things when labels are not visible, why does some tasks don't allow me to change the task type and some other properties, what does it mean when I set my Task Days to 1 day a week, and there's a setting right below saying 1 time/day? What does the numbers at the bottom mean? Why is the stats icon a star, which commonly means "favorite" in the industry? What does "upcoming" task even mean, I have 24 habits and I they don't need to follow a specific order, I just need to make sure I do them. The litmus test for good design is "do they need a manual for this"? And you ABSOLUTELY need the manual for more than half of the features. - Stats are only limited to the page you're viewing, I need an overall view (again, why do we have pages?). Also you can't view the actual values on the graph, which renders them useless, you're just looking at random bumps... What does the "time graph" even mean? Is it an average of every day?  - Limits you to only a maximum of 24 habits. I already filled it up and can't add more... - App timers are not syncing across devices unless you stop it on one and refresh it on the other, and sometimes it doesn't work at all - You can't connect a shortcut to a "timer stopped" action for timers. This is really bad because I can't turn off my Focus mode automatically when the timer is done - When you connect a shortcut, it opens the Shortcuts App every time the action is triggered, which is really annoying - Multiple timers can be started together, which is pretty bad since I want other timers to stop when I start a different timer. Sometimes I forget to stop the other timers and it skews the data - Data exports don't contain your Apple Health stats - There's no RPC APIs (just callback URLs) I can use to integrate my habits or stats with my Obsidian notes  Pretty sure I forgot many other annoyances I have, but all these improvements are listed simply because I love the app and I can see the potential if the gaps are filled. Many thanks to all the people involved in making this app, and I truly hope to see the app in a better place soon.

app: 48. Strides - Habit Tracker + Goals - Goal Planner & Daily Checklist
text: Essential app for tracking habits, best out of many I’ve used || I felt like I had to write an actual review to give this app some more support. Habit tracking apps don’t get nearly the press coverage of todo list apps, document and note apps, cloud storage apps, or even photo filter apps. This is so unfortunate, because tracking your repeated actions and adjusting them, is one of the most powerful ways to shape your life.   I think that habits environment and identity are interwoven, and collectively determine the course of our lives.   This app is the best I’ve found for tracking repetitions and other important quantities (besides YNAB which I use to budget, and Mynetdiary which I use for calorie tracking).  For me there are a few killer features that make Strides stand head and shoulders above all the other habit apps I’ve tried.  - The ability to track multiple reps in the same day, which is so crucial for actually shaping the day - A webapp that has mobile and desktop UIs, and allows Strides to be used on any device with a web browser, including my android phone. (If you’ve never tried the webapp, I def suggest you check it out. I actually have come to prefer using the webapp on the iPad because the desktop UI is simultaneously cleaner in some respects, and also easier to work with imo). The only thing you miss it on from the webapp seems to be reminders. Not a big deal for me, as I actually tend to use apps like ticktick (best task/todo list app imo) for reminders. - Tags. I don’t have to say much here, just look at most habit apps and notice that they don’t have a way to easily group and filter habits, other than simple color labels. That’s fine if you have only a few habits, but if you really track a lot of things that are important to your life, sooner or later you will want to group and filter the habits so you can focus on a select few.   Love the Strides app, I’ve been a subscriber since I switched to it from habit bull (which I think is the closest to strides, but lacked the tags and the the webapp, but did at least have multi rep tracking and apps for android and iOS, the apps didn’t like to sync across iOS and android for me very well however).  Very eager to see if they can add some better views for seeing all habits over the course of the week, and other reporting options.

text: It’s great. Pay them for their hard work if you find it useful. || NOTE: being mad an app isn’t free is like being mad restaurants aren’t free or your plumber isn’t free. I guarantee you that hundreds, if not thousands of hours went into making this app, and it’s updated constantly… which means they’re working on it all the time. If you value someone’s work, you should pay them for it. Having a concentration app shoving ads in your face constantly worlds kind of defeat the purpose, no? Regarding the app: I needed a relatively simple app to break my day into blocks of repeatable tasks (e.g. morning routine) and blocks of time where I could use my existing task management tools to get things done. This app is great for that. Not as rigid as Tiimo time-wise but it’s heavier on reminders. Tiimo ended up being a place where I could see whatever it was that I’d been falling to work on for the past hour… this does a better job of keeping me on track. Support (might be a one person project?) is responsive and useful. Syncing for the watch is excellent while in a routine (another thing Tiimo was terrible at)    -Wishes- Base Functionality: * Halfway reminders, or reminders every 𝑛 minutes would be super useful. While I’m working, I use an interval timer app that gives me a simple notification every six minutes. Having this integrated would be helpful. * would love a mode where I had a pile of tasks and a set block of time and I could choose which ones to do next. Sometimes it doesn’t matter if I shave before a brush my teeth but just need to be reminded to do both and stay on task. UI improvements: * Having text search of emoji would help. Doesn’t have to be any more complicated than a filter based on characters included in the name. Figuring out whether the icon I want is in default or whatever can be tedious. “Wait… was there a work category? No? Maybe electronics? No… hmmm” * Having sub-headings or details under title for tasks would be helpful. * Still not really sure what contexts are. My first guess is that they’d be like GTD contexts like “on the phone,” or “at work,” but that doesn’t really make sense for a scheduled task. Maybe that’s not the right word for the functionality? If so, some other wording could use cleanup— “you can restart at any time” implies that you’re starting from the beginning. Unless I’m not seeing the ability to restart, it should read “you can continue any time.” In think there are a few other minor ones but clearly not important enough to matter. * Would love to see a breakdown of how much time I allocated to each task in reality so I can adjust my schedule or habits. That is more important info to me than whether or not I completed the entire block exactly as prescribed. Thanks for making the app.

text: Not a lot of bells & whistles for the price || I’m updating my review here, because I’ve figured out all of the issues that I was having. I use this app everyday now, and it helps me focus on what’s important, so I do recommend it. The syncing is working great now, and the lagging only seemed to occur when I created my routines. So, I’m changing my review from 4 to 5 stars.  Old review: Unlike many who have complained, I actually did subscribe to the annual subscription, and I get that the goal here is simplicity. But, simple design does not mean less features / functionality. The huge disappointment for me is that you can’t turn off the text-to-speech when a task runs over! I listen to audiobooks during my morning routine and I guess I’m going to have to run this on my iPad in the bathroom while my phone plays my audio, because there is no way to keep it from interrupting. If I had realized this before subscribing, I would not have subscribed. But, there aren’t really any other apps like this. In the past, I used apps like Seconds and MyIntervals, which are for creating workouts. They have way more options within each routine, and I don’t care about summaries or tracking overall progress. I do not have ADHD, nor am I neurodivergent - I just like to be organized. I do have depression and productivity apps help motivate me and keep me focused, so I do rely on them. I turned off the chatbot, which was annoying, and I’m glad that option was available, but there need to be more ways to customize. And, I agree that that the lag times are perplexing. When scrolling, it often freezes and you have to wait for it to “think”. I turned off all the automatic switches from one task to the next (took forever to do because of lag), hoping it would stop talking, but with no luck. It literally announces that the last task has ended automatically, in full, and that the next task has started, in full. Then, it keep nagging every minute over or so, too, even if I pause the routine! I have all routines set to silent with no automatic tasks and I cannot believe the text-to-speech is still so disruptive. I don’t even want it to beep - I just want to check the task when I’m done. I guess I can go make all the tasks way longer so I always complete the task within the timeframe, but I kind of wanted something with close to accurate times to push me - that was the point. Then, I guess I can just stop the routine if I need to stop to do something else for a few minutes, but how inconvenient, and who knows if it’s going to work properly, like save my previous tasks. It seems like whoever made this had a particular goal or vision , which is good, but the code and technical design needs work. I will say that it’s pretty reliable if the app gets closed or exited or anything, about keeping the time going. Any edits to routines get synced well to iCloud, but it doesn’t always sync daily progress between devices.
